summary: The candidate commit unifies the previously dual-layer T033 contract (FROZEN_FROM_BASELINE_6C31778 marker plus a separate Owner amendment block) into a single contract body. The top-of-file `Contract status: FROZEN_FROM_BASELINE_6C31778` line is removed; the body that previously carried only the 5-line baseline summary is replaced with fully expanded Outcome, Deliverables, Acceptance, Must-not, and References sections that absorb every binding clause from Owner decision #3 (Robinhood finality policy) and Owner decision #7 (FINALIZED_ANCESTRY_VIOLATION critical incident). The Outcome declares that the RPC finalized tag is the formal finality boundary, defines the unfinalized window as `finalized + 1` to `latest` (observable but never promoted to the qualified dataset), and reaffirms append-only finalized raw evidence. Deliverables specify a configurable finality policy with explicit injection in tests, a fail-closed stance on finalized unavailability/fallback/error/qualified-endpoint ancestry disagreement, the `confirmations = 12` retention as an `EXPERIMENTAL_NOT_LIVE_APPROVED` placeholder, the full reason-code set (`finalized_unavailable`, `finalized_ancestry_disagreement`, `finality_tag_unavailable`, `FINALIZED_ANCESTRY_VIOLATION`), common-ancestor search with orphan marking/replacement that preserves orphan raw bytes, a deep-reorg halt that records an append-only critical-incident candidate, the reorg journal, and the append-only critical-incident candidate recorder. Acceptance codifies the shallow/deep reorg fixtures, provider disagreement halt with `finalized_ancestry_disagreement`, removed-log fixture, orphan-reappearance fixture, finalized-data append-only guarantee with superseding-generation-after-operator-review only, explicit test injection of the finality policy, the `confirmations = 12` placeholder-only constraint, fail-closed on finalized unavailability/fallback/error/ancestry disagreement, the full `FINALIZED_ANCESTRY_VIOLATION` response (halt, append-only critical-incident candidate, block new backtest qualification/paper/live, preserve old raw partitions/canonical generation/provider evidence, persist new fork/observation as new append-only evidence, escalate to Phase 8, superseding canonical generation only after human incident declaration and re-checking), the exact required sentence `Finalized raw evidence is never rewritten, including during a critical incident. A declared critical incident may authorize creation of a superseding canonical generation after operator review.`, and the four reason codes as distinct manifest entries. Must-not includes every required prohibition: no equating confirmations with finality across chains, no deleting orphan raw logs, no continuing decisions during unresolved ancestry (including finalized ancestry disagreement or any pending critical-incident candidate), no overwriting/deleting/in-place-rewriting finalized raw evidence at any time including during a critical incident, no automatic fallback to a fixed confirmations count, no using `confirmations = 12` for mainnet qualification/paper/live promotion, and no performing Phase 8 operator/incident handling inside T033. References still cite R9 and R10, and the new `Binding direction reference` subsection at the end of the file is explicitly framed as an audit trail only, not a second source of binding direction, citing the recorded `/tmp/owner_decision_T033.txt` source and Decisions 3, 5, and 7. ADR-010 / ADR-011 consistency: the finalized-tag boundary plus qualified-endpoint ancestry-disagreement halt aligns with ADR-010's capability-driven routing (each endpoint's supported finality tag and finalized ancestry are observable provider capabilities; an irreducible provider disagreement prevents dataset qualification, and the cross-endpoint check is not claimed as infrastructure independence), and ADR-011's explicit test-injection principle is reflected by the requirement that every finality/reorg test must inject an explicit finality policy rather than rely on a production default. Path compliance: the only contract change is in `todo/phases/P03-ingestion-and-storage/T033.md`; the other two tracked files (`todo/config.yaml` workflow_state/status flip from PLANNING to AWAITING_PLAN_REVIEW, and `todo/evidence/P03/T033/attempt-001-planner.json` planner handoff) are mechanical outputs of the planning workflow and do not alter task status, attempt counter, evidence pointer, commit SHA, runtime model, approval metadata, controller code, another task contract, docs/intent, or docs/spec. Executability: with the unified contract body in place, a Developer entering attempt 002 has exactly one binding contract body to implement against; all Acceptance clauses remain at the level Developer attempt 001 already triaged to, and no Acceptance clause was weakened or removed to fit the merge.
